metric: # One row per promise the design makes about the hands. metric is a name from measure.json (report.py lists them); min and max bound it (either may be empty); unit is what the report prints; why is the sentence in the design it comes from. reference/targets.md says how to turn an adjective into a row. These are the first project's.

why: DESIGN.md 3.1: coyote time about 0.1 s. The pressable window runs two frames under the knob (the walk-off frame and the zero boundary each cost one)
DESIGN.md 3.1: instant turn. A reversal whose velocity crosses zero inside four frames reads as instant; one frame would be a snap
DESIGN.md 3.1: slight acceleration. Under a fifth of a second to top speed and more than one frame
DESIGN.md 3.1: slight deceleration. A released stick stops inside a few frames and not on the spot
the jump is authored at 0.36 s to the apex: springy not floaty
the jump is authored at 168 px (2.8 tiles of 60) so a three-tile ledge is a wall; the discrete step adds about v0*dt/2
the fall multiplier is 1.6: the fall is quicker than the rise and the jump lands with weight
variable height: a one-frame tap hops clearly under half the full jump
the dash is a 0.16 s commitment: a step and not a cutscene
design.md pillars: the jump-cancelled dash. A jump pressed almost anywhere in the dash fires at its end; the first frame or two may be lost to the buffer
no landing lag: the run is back at speed on touchdown
the slide is authored at 120 px/s: a wall is a place to think
DESIGN.md 3.1 (2026-09-15): a single wall is a slow ladder at under a wall jump's height (144 px) per second
docs/combat/damage-pipeline.md: light hitstop 2 frames; short or it is lag
docs/combat/damage-pipeline.md: heavy hitstop 4 frames; the difference from light is the weight
docs/combat/damage-pipeline.md: player knockback is loss of control on a small budget
